title: Relative logarithmic charts for a marked nodal curve over a smooth pair
statement: Let $F$ be any field [def-weil-field], $Y$ an integral smooth finite-type $F$-scheme, and $E$ a relative strict normal crossings divisor on $Y/F$ [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-trf-smooth-strict-normal-crossings-divisor]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be proper, flat and finitely presented, with $X$ Noetherian and of finite type over $F$, with nonempty connected reduced one-dimensional nodal geometric fibres, and smooth over $Y\setminus|E|$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres]. Let $N\hookrightarrow X$ be a finite disjoint union of sections in the relative smooth locus [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Put $B=|N|\cup g^{-1}|E|$ and $U=X\setminus B$. Then $N$ is an effective Cartier divisor, finite etale over $Y$, $B$ is nowhere dense, and the divisorial log structures of $(Y,|E|)$ and $(X,B)$ are fine saturated and log regular [def-trf-log-regular-pair, def-trf-fs-log-blowup, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Their triviality loci are respectively $Y\setminus|E|$ and $U$. The morphisms $(X,B)\to(Y,|E|)$ and $(Y,|E|)\to(\operatorname{Spec}F,F^\times)$, hence also their composite, are log smooth in the chart sense [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. More precisely, etale locally on source and base, at a node there is a base chart $P$ and an equation $uv=\varepsilon\alpha(a)$ with $a\in P$, a unit $\varepsilon$, and chart map $R=\mathbf Z\oplus P\to Q=\mathbf N^2\amalg_{\mathbf N}R$, where $1\mapsto(1,1)$ and $1\mapsto(1,a)$ define the pushout. The group-completion map is injective with cokernel $\mathbf Z$, and the scheme comparison for this chart is etale. At a smooth unmarked point the chart map is $P\to P$ with smooth comparison; at a marked point it is $P\to P\oplus\mathbf N$ with etale comparison and marking equation $z=0$. These charts give the stated divisorial log structures. Empty $E$ or $N$ is allowed, and no perfection assumption on $F$ is made. Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth].

proof.text: The effective Cartier divisor $E$ has dense open complement: on the integral scheme $Y$ its local equation is a nonzero element and hence does not vanish at the generic point. Apply the converse of [lem-sfb-free-characteristic-relative-nc-criterion] to $(Y,|E|)$. It gives the divisorial fs log structure, log regularity, triviality locus $Y\setminus|E|$, and log smoothness over the trivial log field, over this very field $F$. In particular the cited result does not require $F$ perfect or algebraically closed. The scheme $Y$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field is Noetherian; $X$ is Noetherian by hypothesis.

source.place: VI 1.4--1.5(i), pp.69--70; X Lemma 2.2 proof, p.149, relative smooth-pair remark

proof.text: As a $Y$-scheme $N$ is a finite disjoint union of copies of $Y$, because its components are sections. Thus $N\to Y$ is finite etale (on affine inverse images its algebra is a finite product of copies of the base algebra). To check its Cartier ideal, work near one section and avoid the other, disjoint, sections. Apply [lem-pur-smooth-pair-local-coordinates] over $S=Y$ to this section in the relative smooth locus of $X$. The section has relative dimension zero and the ambient smooth curve has relative dimension one, so the coordinate description has $a=0,b=1$. Its ideal is generated by the regular coordinate $z$, a non-zero-divisor. Off $N$ the ideal is the unit ideal; therefore $N$ is an effective Cartier divisor, also when empty. These are precisely the Cartier and etale marking hypotheses required by the nodal normal-form lemma.

source.place: Tag 0FUE, more-morphisms.tex, lemma-etale-local-structure, and its regular-sequence conclusion

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-nodal-etale-chart] to $g$, the log regular base from step 1, and $D=N$ from step 2. Its flatness, local finite presentation, nodal connected one-dimensional geometric fibres and smoothness off $|E|$ are all explicit hypotheses here. At a node it supplies etale neighbourhoods, disjoint from $N$, the equation $uv=h$, a base fs chart $P$, and $h=\varepsilon\alpha(a)$ with $a\in P$. By [lem-trf-nodal-divisorial-chart], $R=\mathbf Z\oplus P$ and $Q=\mathbf N^2\amalg_{\mathbf N}R$ are fs and $R\to Q$ has injective group map with cokernel $\mathbf Z$. Map the integer generator to $\varepsilon$ and the two branch generators to $u,v$. The monoid-algebra isomorphism in that lemma identifies the chart comparison target with $uv=\varepsilon\alpha(a)$, so the comparison is the etale morphism just obtained. The additional $\mathbf Z$ maps to units, so $R$ is still a chart of the original base log structure. Form the source log structure associated to $Q\to\mathcal O_X$ using [lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks]; the compatible map from $R$ gives a morphism to the base log scheme.

source.place: VI Proposition 1.9 proof, p.71, equation (1.a) and the two displayed squares

proof.text: At a smooth unmarked point the same normal-form lemma gives a neighbourhood avoiding $N$ and a smooth morphism to the base. Use the base chart $P\to P$ and its associated log structure. Its comparison is the given smooth morphism and its group cokernel is zero. At a marked point the lemma gives an etale map to $\mathbf A^1_Y$, with $N$ exactly $z=0$. Use $P\to P\oplus\mathbf N$, mapping the added generator to $z$; the comparison is this etale map and its group cokernel is $\mathbf Z$. The monoids $P\oplus\mathbf N$ are fs directly from the definition, component by component. The associated-log construction and its universal property supply the compatible log morphisms in both cases. At nodes step 3 gives the same chart properties. Thus every local log morphism is log smooth by [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]: the kernel and torsion subgroup of the cokernel are zero, of order one invertible in every characteristic.

source.place: VI Proposition 1.9 proof, pp.70--71, smooth-locus case and injective-chart test

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-log-smooth-log-regular] to each local log scheme just constructed: the base is log regular, its group maps are injective with torsion-free cokernel, and comparisons are smooth or etale. It makes the local structure log regular, with dense triviality locus and equal to the divisorial structure of that locus. Compute this locus before making the identification. For an associated log chart the stalk is trivial exactly when every chart generator maps to a unit, by the stalk formula in [lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks]. At a smooth unmarked point this says that the base chart is trivial, hence the point lies off $g^{-1}|E|$. At a marking it says this and $z$ is a unit, hence also that the point is off $N$. At a node the generators are $u,v$ and $R$: if the base chart is trivial then $h=\varepsilon\alpha(a)$ is a unit, and $uv=h$ forces both $u,v$ to be units. Conversely triviality forces every base generator to be a unit. These node neighbourhoods avoid $N$. Consequently in every case the triviality locus is exactly $U=X\setminus(|N|\cup g^{-1}|E|)$. The recovered divisorial structures are therefore all restrictions of the single sheaf $\mathcal O_X\cap j_*\mathcal O_U^\times$. This proves that $U$ is dense, $B$ nowhere dense, and that this sheaf is fs log regular. The local log morphisms agree on overlaps: their structure maps are the inclusions of divisorial functions and the map from the base is pullback of those functions. Hence they define the asserted global divisorial log morphism.

source.place: VI 1.4 and 1.8, pp.69--70; Proposition 1.9 proof, p.71, divisorial identification

proof.text: The charts of steps 3--5 now are charts for the stated divisorial structures, so $g$ is log smooth by the chart definition [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. Step 1 already proved $(Y,|E|)\to(\operatorname{Spec}F,F^\times)$ log smooth. Their composite is log smooth by [lem-sfb-log-smooth-composition-strict-base-change]. When $E$ is empty the base chart can be $0$; the smoothness hypothesis then leaves no nodes. When $N$ is empty there are no marked charts. Empty markings still have the Cartier unit ideal. The group computations have no torsion, so no restriction on the characteristic or perfection of $F$ has entered.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q129-c52bf3e11 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Q129 c52bf3e1: one commit, item-only split with no new nodes. Statement, source and stmt_deps are unchanged from earlier snapshots. Proof_deps equal the union of uses, there is no cycle and there is no SGA citation. Read ILO VI 1.4-1.9 (pp.70-71). The item is VI 1.9 for an integral smooth Y over any field F with an SNC divisor E, plus base log smoothness over F (X 2.2 remark). Its charts match the source exactly: R=Z+P, Q the pushout by 1->(1,1) and 1->(1,a), Z->eps. Step 1: the converse of the free-characteristic nc-criterion applies for any field. E has dense complement because its non-zero-divisor generator on integral Y does not vanish at the generic point. Y is Noetherian. Step 2: smooth-pair coordinates over S=Y on the open smooth locus give a=0, b=1, so each section is cut out by one non-zero-divisor. Together with finite etaleness of N, this gives the Cartier ideal and etale marking that lem-trf-nodal-etale-chart needs; all its hypotheses hold. Step 3: the divisorial-chart node's monoid-ring isomorphism makes the comparison morphism the given etale map. R is a chart because the Z factor maps to units. Step 4: P->P (smooth comparison) and P->P+N (etale comparison), with no kernel and torsion-free cokernel. Step 5: log-smooth=>log-regular is applied per chart, with all hypotheses checked. By the stalk formula the triviality locus is exactly X\B (at a node, uv=h with h a unit forces u and v to be units), so the local structures are restrictions of the divisorial sheaf and the morphism glues by pullback of functions. Step 6: the charts cover X, and the composition node gives the composite. Edge cases checked: E or N empty, uv=t^m, imperfect F, several branches meeting. Batch-5: all 7 flagged citations are generic log-geometry or commutative-algebra tools (Kato, ILO VI, Stacks 0CBY/046Y) or definitions, not trace-formula or Poincare-duality content, so they are accepted.
